51555370.protein: Inactive tyrosine-protein kinase transmembrane receptor ROR1
51555370.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to full length human His-tagged ROR1 (937 residues ) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis Section: SPR studies with 39 peptides confirmed three hit series of macrocyclic peptides as tight binders from our initial selections (Fig. 2). Compounds 1–3 are exemplars from these three series, exhibiting concentration-dependent binding to hROR1-His with nanomolar affinity (See Fig. S1). Compounds 1 and 3 fit well to a 1:1 Langmuir model as did most of the 39 hits, but Compound 2 showed different binding kinetics in the SPR studies. Compounds also showed binding, albeit weaker, to hROR2-ECD, as all peptides showed significantly faster dissociation rates than against hROR1. The ROR1/ROR2 selectivity profile was series dependent. Sequence identity between canonical sequences of full length human ROR1 (937 aa) and ROR2 (943 aa) is 56.4 % overall, but in the ECD regions (hROR1 = 1–406; hROR2 = 1–403) rises to 60.8 % identity, with the overall highest similarity between the respective CRDs (77.6 % identity).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 Caption: Fig. 2. Three hit series and representative peptides and SPR data vs. hROR1-His and hROR2-His.
